questions.question: In the figure, △ABC and △PQR have AB = PQ = 6 cm, BC = QR = 8 cm and CA = RP = 7 cm. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PQR. Hence find the length (in cm) of side corresponding to BC under this congruence.
questions.method_hint: SSS: three corresponding sides equal ⇒ triangles congruent; corresponding sides then equal by CPCT.
questions.explanation: AB=PQ, BC=QR, CA=RP. By SSS, △ABC ≅ △PQR with B↔Q. So BC corresponds to QR = 8.

questions.question: In the figure, two plane figures match under a flip so that every point of one maps onto the other. If the perimeter of the first figure is 42 cm, find the perimeter (in cm) of its congruent twin.
questions.method_hint: Congruent figures have the same shape and size, so corresponding lengths and perimeters are equal.
questions.explanation: Congruent figures have equal corresponding sides, so perimeters are equal. Perimeter = 42.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △DEF under A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. If ∠A = 55° and ∠B = 70°, find ∠F in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Under congruence, corresponding angles are equal (CPCT). C↔F so ∠C = ∠F. Also ∠A+∠B+∠C=180°.

questions.question: In the figure, a rubber stamp prints congruent copies of a triangle. One print has base 9 cm. Find the base (in cm) of the next congruent print of the same stamp.
questions.method_hint: Congruent copies from the same stamp have equal corresponding lengths.
questions.explanation: Congruent figures produced by the same stamp are equal in all corresponding lengths. Base = 9.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △XYZ. If AB = 5.5 cm and the side corresponding to AB is XY, find XY in cm.
questions.method_hint: Corresponding sides of congruent triangles are equal.
questions.explanation: Under △ABC ≅ △XYZ with A↔X, B↔Y, AB corresponds to XY, so XY = 5.5.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △PQR and also △ABC ≅ △XYZ. If PQ = 11 cm, find the length (in cm) of the side of △XYZ that corresponds to AB (same correspondence A↔P↔X, B↔Q↔Y).
questions.method_hint: Congruence is transitive for corresponding parts: if both are congruent to △ABC under matching letters, corresponding sides match.
questions.explanation: AB corresponds to PQ and to XY. PQ = 11 ⇒ XY = 11.

questions.question: In the figure, square ABCD has diagonal AC. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △ADC. Hence find ∠BAC + ∠DAC in degrees (the full angle at A of the square).
questions.method_hint: In a square all sides are equal and diagonals create two triangles with three equal sides (SSS).
questions.explanation: AB=AD, BC=DC, AC common ⇒ SSS ⇒ △ABC ≅ △ADC. ∠BAD of a square is 90°, so ∠BAC+∠DAC = 90.

questions.question: In the figure, two congruent rectangles each measure 12 cm by 5 cm. Find the total area (in cm²) of both rectangles together.
questions.method_hint: Area of rectangle = length × breadth. Congruent rectangles have equal areas.
questions.explanation: Each area = 12×5 = 60. Both together = 120.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △DEF. The map of vertices is A↔D, B↔E, C↔F. If BC = 3/4 of AC and AC = 16 cm, find DE in cm when AB = AC − 4.
questions.method_hint: Find AB from AC, then use corresponding sides under the given vertex map.
questions.explanation: AB = 16 − 4 = 12. A↔D, B↔E ⇒ AB corresponds to DE, so DE = 12.

questions.question: In the figure, a cardboard triangle is flipped and placed on another triangle so every vertex matches. If the original has angles 40°, 60° and 80°, find the largest angle (in degrees) of the congruent twin.
questions.method_hint: Flipping preserves size of angles; corresponding angles remain equal.
questions.explanation: Congruent twin has the same angles 40°, 60°, 80°. Largest = 80.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = CD = 7 cm and PQ = RS. If PQ = AB, find RS in cm.
questions.method_hint: Congruent (equal) line segments have equal lengths; equality is transitive.
questions.explanation: PQ = AB = 7 and PQ = RS ⇒ RS = 7.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠AOB ≅ ∠QPR. If ∠AOB = 48°, find ∠QPR in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Congruent angles have equal measures.
questions.explanation: ∠AOB ≅ ∠QPR ⇒ measures equal, so ∠QPR = 48.

questions.question: In the figure, ray OX bisects ∠AOB. If ∠AOX = 35°, find ∠AOB in degrees.
questions.method_hint: An angle bisector divides an angle into two congruent (equal) angles.
questions.explanation: ∠AOX = ∠XOB = 35 ⇒ ∠AOB = 70.

questions.question: In the figure, M is the midpoint of AB. If AM = 9/2 cm, find AB in cm.
questions.method_hint: Midpoint divides a segment into two congruent halves of equal length.
questions.explanation: AM = MB = 9/2 ⇒ AB = 9.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠1 ≅ ∠2 and ∠2 ≅ ∠3. If ∠1 = 62°, find ∠3 in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Congruence of angles is transitive.

questions.question: In the figure, AB ≅ CD and CD ≅ EF. Points divide AB into three congruent parts each of length 4 cm. Find EF in cm.
questions.method_hint: Equal segments have equal lengths; sum of three congruent parts gives the whole.
questions.explanation: AB = 3×4 = 12. AB ≅ CD ≅ EF ⇒ EF = 12.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠PQR is bisected by ray QS and also ∠PQS ≅ ∠TUV. If ∠TUV = 27°, find ∠PQR in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Bisector makes two equal halves; congruent angles share measure.
questions.explanation: ∠PQS = ∠TUV = 27 ⇒ half of ∠PQR is 27 ⇒ ∠PQR = 54.

questions.question: Two congruent line segments have lengths x cm and (x + 3) cm and together measure 25 cm. Find the longer length in cm.
questions.method_hint: For two segments: x + (x + 3) = 25. Solve for x, then longer = x + 3.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠A = ∠B and ∠B = ∠C. If ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180° (angles of a triangle), find ∠A in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Equal angles in a triangle that sum to 180° are each 60° when all three are equal.
questions.explanation: ∠A=∠B=∠C and sum 180 ⇒ each is 60.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = 2·CM where M is midpoint of AB and CM is drawn to a point C off the line. If CM = 5 cm, find AB in cm.
questions.method_hint: Midpoint fact is about AM and MB; here AB = 2·CM is an extra given length relation.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = PQ, BC = QR and CA = RP. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PQR by SSS. If AB = 6 cm, find PQ in cm.
questions.method_hint: SSS criterion: three sides of one triangle equal to three corresponding sides of the other.
questions.explanation: Given three pairs of equal sides ⇒ SSS ⇒ △ABC ≅ △PQR ⇒ PQ = AB = 6.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = DE, ∠B = ∠E and BC = EF. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △DEF by SAS. If ∠B = 50°, find ∠E in degrees.
questions.method_hint: SAS: two sides and the included angle equal.
questions.explanation: AB, ∠B, BC match DE, ∠E, EF with included angles ⇒ SAS. ∠E = ∠B = 50.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = AD, CB = CD. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △ADC by SSS. If AB = 9 cm, find AD in cm.
questions.method_hint: Include the common side AC; then SSS applies.
questions.explanation: AB=AD, CB=CD, AC common ⇒ SSS ⇒ △ABC ≅ △ADC ⇒ AD = AB = 9.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC and △DBC share side BC with AB = DB and AC = DC. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △DBC by SSS. If AC = 10 cm, find DC in cm.
questions.method_hint: Shared side BC is common; use SSS with the two given equal pairs.
questions.explanation: AB=DB, AC=DC, BC common ⇒ SSS. DC = AC = 10.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = XY = 6 cm, AC = XZ = 5 cm and ∠A = ∠X = 30° (included). Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △XYZ by SAS. Find ∠X in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Included angle lies between the two equal sides.
questions.explanation: Two sides and included angle equal ⇒ SAS. ∠X = 30.

questions.question: In the figure, O is midpoint of AD and of BC. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △AOB ≅ △DOC by SAS (use vertical angles). If AO = 7 cm, find OD in cm.
questions.method_hint: Midpoint ⇒ AO=OD and BO=OC; vertical angles at O are equal — that included angle gives SAS.
questions.explanation: AO=OD, ∠AOB=∠DOC (vert. opp.), BO=OC ⇒ SAS. OD = AO = 7.

questions.question: In the figure, AB = DE, BC = EF and AC = DF. A student claims SSA proves congruence. If the only valid criterion that fits the three equal sides is SSS, write 1 for SSS and 0 for SSA. What number should the student choose?
questions.method_hint: SSA does not guarantee congruence; three sides do (SSS).
questions.explanation: Three sides equal ⇒ SSS (code 1), not SSA.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC has AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm, ∠B = 90°. △PQR has PQ = 8 cm, QR = 6 cm, ∠Q = 90°. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove congruence by SAS. Find AB + PQ in cm.
questions.method_hint: Right angle is included between AB,BC and PQ,QR respectively.
questions.explanation: AB=PQ, ∠B=∠Q=90°, BC=QR ⇒ SAS. AB+PQ = 8+8 = 16.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △ADC by SSS with AC common. If ∠BAC = 35°, find ∠DAC in degrees.
questions.method_hint: CPCT: corresponding angles at A are equal when B↔D under △ABC ≅ △ADC.
questions.explanation: △ABC ≅ △ADC with B↔D ⇒ ∠BAC = ∠DAC = 35.

questions.question: In the figure, sides of △ABC are 3.5 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm. △JAM has the same three side lengths. Find the number of distinct SSS correspondences that make △ABC ≅ △JAM when vertices are matched by equal side lengths (enter how many valid letter maps exist among the 6 permutations that preserve side matching — answer is 1 for the unique size-matching map up to naming in the book style, use 1).
questions.method_hint: SSS gives congruence once corresponding equal sides are matched; there is essentially one geometric match of the three lengths.
questions.explanation: Three distinct side lengths determine a unique correspondence of vertices by matching lengths, so 1.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠B = ∠Q, BC = QR and ∠C = ∠R. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PQR by ASA. If BC = 5 cm, find QR in cm.
questions.method_hint: ASA: two angles and the included side.
questions.explanation: ∠B, BC, ∠C match ∠Q, QR, ∠R ⇒ ASA. QR = BC = 5.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC and △PQR are right-angled at B and Q with hypotenuse AC = PR and leg AB = PQ. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PQR by RHS. If AB = 9 cm, find PQ in cm.
questions.method_hint: RHS: right angle, hypotenuse and one side.
questions.explanation: Right angles at B,Q; AC=PR; AB=PQ ⇒ RHS. PQ = 9.

questions.question: In the figure, AB ∥ CD, AB = CD, and O is intersection of AC and BD. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △AOB ≅ △COD by ASA. If AB = 10 cm, find CD in cm.
questions.method_hint: Parallel lines give alternate interior angles equal; AB=CD is the included side pair with those angles.
questions.explanation: Alternate angles equal and AB=CD ⇒ ASA. CD = AB = 10.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC and △DCB are right-angled at B and C respectively with AB = DC and BC common. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △DCB by RHS (or SAS). If AB = 12 cm, find DC in cm.
questions.method_hint: Right angles at B and C; hypotenuse AC and DB; given AB=DC and common BC.
questions.explanation: AB = DC given; with right angles and common/hypotenuse setup ⇒ congruence. DC = 12.

questions.question: In the figure, ∠A = ∠P = 40°, ∠B = ∠Q = 70°, and side AB = PQ (included between ∠A,∠B and ∠P,∠Q). Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PQR by ASA. Find ∠C in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Third angle of a triangle is 180° minus the other two; ASA uses two angles and included side.
questions.explanation: ∠C = 180−40−70 = 70. (ASA proves congruence; CPCT also gives ∠C=∠R=70.)

questions.question: In the figure, altitude AB is drawn from A to side CD of △ACD with B on CD and CB = BD. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △ABD by RHS (or SAS). If ∠CAB = 28°, find ∠DAB in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Altitude ⇒ right angles at B; AB common hypotenuse relative to the small right triangles; CB=BD.
questions.explanation: Right angles at B, AB common, CB=BD ⇒ RHS. ∠CAB=∠DAB by CPCT = 28.

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC ≅ △PQR by ASA. If ∠A = 55° and ∠B = 65°, find ∠R in degrees.
questions.method_hint: Find ∠C first from angle sum; under A↔P, B↔Q, C↔R, ∠C corresponds to ∠R.

questions.question: In the figure, two right triangles have equal hypotenuses 13 cm and one pair of equal legs 5 cm. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove they are congruent by RHS. Find the other leg in cm (use Pythagoras).
questions.method_hint: RHS gives congruence; Pythagoras: other² + 5² = 13².

questions.question: In the figure, △ABC and △PBC overlap on BC with ∠ABC = ∠PCB and ∠ACB = ∠PBC. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △PCB by ASA. If BC = 14 cm, find the length of the common side used as included side in cm.
questions.method_hint: The included side between the equal angle pairs is the common side BC.
questions.explanation: ASA uses included side BC = 14.

questions.question: In the figure, rectangle ABCD has ∠ABC = ∠BCD = 90° and AB = DC. Write using: (1) To prove (2) Diagram with congruent marks (3) Condition–Reason table with 3 rows (4) Congruence criterion. Prove △ABC ≅ △DCB. If BC = 15 cm, find CB in cm (same segment).
questions.method_hint: Right angles at B and C, AB=DC, BC common ⇒ RHS/SAS.
questions.explanation: BC is common, so its length is 15.
